name: Sisera
bio:
Sisera was the commander of the army of Jabin, king of Canaan, stationed at Harosheth Haggoyim, who oppressed Israel for twenty years with nine hundred iron chariots. The prophetess Deborah, under the LORD's command, summoned Barak to lead ten thousand Israelites to Mount Tabor, where the LORD routed Sisera's entire army before Barak, forcing Sisera to abandon his chariot and flee on foot (Judges 4:1-16).

Sisera fled to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite. Jael came out to meet him, saying, "Come, my lord, come right in. Don't be afraid," and gave him milk to drink instead of water, covering him as he rested. Sisera asked her to lie on his behalf if anyone came looking for him, then fell into an exhausted sleep. While he slept, Jael took a tent peg and a hammer, crept up quietly, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground, killing him (Judges 4:17-21). When Barak arrived in pursuit, Jael brought him into the tent to show him Sisera lying dead with the tent peg through his temple. Sisera's defeat and death became the central victory celebrated in the song of Judges 5.
